questions.question: When and by how many states were the Sustainable Development Goals adopted?
options: In 2015, by all 193 UN member states
questions.explanation: In September 2015 all 193 UN member states adopted the 2030 Agenda with its 17 SDGs.

questions.question: How many Sustainable Development Goals are there?
questions.explanation: There are 17 Sustainable Development Goals with 169 specific targets.

questions.question: How do the SDGs differ from the earlier Millennium Development Goals?
options: The SDGs apply to ALL countries, not just developing ones
The SDGs apply only to poor countries
questions.explanation: Unlike the MDGs, the SDGs are universal — they apply to all countries, rich and poor.

questions.question: What does it mean that the SDGs are "interconnected"?
options: Progress on one goal often supports progress on others
Only one goal can be pursued at a time
questions.explanation: The SDGs are integrated and indivisible: progress on one (e.g. education) often supports others (e.g. poverty reduction).

questions.question: According to the chapter, where has SDG progress stalled or reversed?
questions.explanation: Progress has stalled or reversed on hunger, climate action, biodiversity and equality, despite gains elsewhere.
